lines.en: No hands are held on the way to the cafe — nor am I able to strike some sort of balance and secretly kiss Uta as well now that Makoto has gotten hers.
But I am able to zone out.
I’m able to focus on each shining star that slowly shows up in that expansive spring sky.
And it leaves me wondering just how far away they are since I know it takes years for the light to reach us sometimes.
I think of Vega. I’m pretty sure that one was the princess. And how her counterpart never deserved her and is better off on the opposite end of the bird bridge.
But if there’s anything I know about anything (there’s not), it’s that she might be somewhere else — holding her hand up to the sky the way she always did.
And thinking the same thing about me.
Or maybe she already is and I’m just too stubborn to accept it. That sounds plausible too.
Especially when her visage lies ten feet in front of me and I have to fight back against the sun’s gravitational pull to not violently crash into her the way I always want to.
I’ll stop soon enough. Maybe even visit the shrine. And maybe I’ll get to a point where I’ll be able to think about her when I’m with her rather than doing it with others.
That’d be nice, I think. Just sitting on a bench somewhere. Maybe eating takoyaki or whatever else she coerced me into buying her.
That aspect of her personality remains the same. I can still feel the sarcasm and desire to drag me around on a leash pouring out of her like carbon dioxide.
Just my memories have become a mask, so they shield me from the byproduct of her loneliness and wind up being lost on me when I close my eyes and pretend I’m lonely too.
I’m not, though.
I’m just sad.
: Welp. Guess it’s about time for you to break off from us and go spend the night with somebody else.
: My money’s on Ami. He started looking for her the moment we walked in.
: I’m just looking around. For no one in particular. And I’ll probably spend the night with Imani since she’s the only one I can talk to without making someone else jealous.
: Imani might be the one we’re most jealous of. She’s the only one who could make out with you in public without getting you into trouble. That’s the real dream, Sensei.
: You might have to look out for Tsuneyo too if that’s the sole metric you’re using to define your jealousy.
: Damn it. I might need to update the ranking at this rate.
: So! How was it getting to spend a good five minutes “alone” with Sensei without him pushing you away?
: It was very nice. Thank you.
: I still think you should have just sucked him off or something. You’re sneaky enough. You could have managed it.
: What’s wrong? Why are you so quiet? This is a good opportunity for us to bond over our greatest mutual interest.
: Because I can’t look at you without seeing him. And that doesn’t feel good when you’re always trying to hurt me now.
: Not always, Maya. I do plenty of nice things for you. Remember?
: Yes, Ami. I remember.
: I just think I liked you a little more before you were a time-jumping psychopath who tied me to chairs and forced me to orgasm for fun.
: You kept orgasming after I untied you too. What’s your excuse there, Maya?
: That I am a shameful pervert who is currently experiencing the largest drought in sexual gratification I have had since I first started fucking your dad.
: Fucking my dad how?
: Doggy. Cowgirl. Reverse cowgirl. Whatever it’s called when you do it in the bath. Ekiben. Backwards spider crawl. Even missionary when we’re feeling really sick.
: Maya-
: The bicycle. The little dipper. Flatiron. Wheelbarrow. Seated wheelbarrow. The standing dragon. The sideways, slanted flatiron wheelbarrow dragon crawl.
: That one isn’t even real.
: I don’t know the name of that one. But whatever it was, it felt really good.
: You were supposed to just say “behind your back.”
: Oh. Yeah. I was fucking your dad behind your back.
: But we’ve already talked about that!
: And you already know I feel bad, so I don’t understand why we’re still stuck on it and not just fucking him together when that was the original plan.
: You know I’d still prefer to have him all to myself, right?
: Yeah. So would literally everyone else. Which I’m pretty sure is why we were going to join forces in the first place.
: You really are an interesting one, Maya. I’m actually almost happy you didn’t get reset.
: I’m very happy I didn’t get reset. I’d just be happier if I was also regularly sleeping with your dad. Which I still intend to do whether you like it or not.
: Are you sure that’s something you want to be telling me?
: See, that’s the thing. I don’t really care.
: I love you and I don’t want to hurt you. Just, at the same time, I also love Sensei and I want him to pierce my cervix with his colossal dad-dick.
: God, it’s like your settings are broken by default. It’s so extremely irritating. But also kind of endearing.
: Thanks. I’ve always taken a lot of pride in being his secret cock-sleeve.
: So where along the line did you gain feelings?
: I don’t know. But if you could use your time powers to go back and prevent it from ever happening, I’d appreciate that a lot. Having feelings sucks.
: I don’t have any powers, Maya.
: I’m just another regular teenage girl...with the worst luck in the world.
: Hey, Senpai! Wasn’t sure if you were joining us here or not. Glad you did, though. Want a drink? It’s on Haruka as part of the sponsorship deal.
: I just ordered one myself. Thanks, though.
: No problem. Also, do you know what’s going on with Nodoka? I’ve barely heard a word out of her all day.
: Which is crazy because she normally has a lot of words and a good portion of them need to be heavily censored.
: Uhh...everything okay, Nodoka? You doing alright?
: I think so. I can’t really tell.
: I have been thinking more about death lately.
: That...does not sound like “alright” to me, Nodoka.
: No, I suppose it wouldn’t.
: I need to go grocery shopping soon.
: Do you want to field this or should I?
: I’ll field it. You go do Dorm Wars stuff.
: On it. We were supposed to start soon anyway. Be right back!
: Nodoka — look at me.
: Did...something happen?
: Yes.
: I think my mother told me she loves me.
: Attention, Koi Cafe and girls of 1-A!
: It’s been a long first day of Dorm Wars — but it ain’t over yet!
: We’ve got one last competition to hold before sending you all back to the hotel to fend for yourselves for the next 24 hours.
: But not without first getting to everybody’s favorite part of any competition — explaining the rules!
: Yay! Regulations!
: No clapping, Yukihime! Regulations on comedy do naught but dilute its potential impact!
: You know, after the last time we did that, I figured that you of all people would be in favor of this, Molly.
: That...oh. Yes. I suppose that...some regulations might be necessary to prevent anyone else from feeling...horribly disgusting.
: Yay! Some regulations!
: Yes, Yasu! Some regulations!
: No inappropriate jokes about teacher-student conduct! Because Senpai and I may be hot commodities, but we’re still people! And people have feelings!
: Crude humor is fine. But keep in mind that nobody wants to hear about anybody covered in semen.
: One last rule. Tsuneyo is not allowed anywhere near the microphone.
: First, you take my costume. Now, you take my freedom. What is next? My body?
: Aaaand the first rule has already been broken!
: But let’s just overlook that because now it’s Futaba’s turn and there’s no way she’d tell any inappropriate jokes! Right, Futaba?!
: Futaba?
: Why don’t you just go ahead and introduce yourself? That’s a good way to get the ball rolling, right?
: Hi.
: Futaba.
: That is name.
: Aight. It appears we may have underestimated the severity of Futaba’s stage fright. So why doesn’t everyone go ahead and cheer her on?! That’ll help, right?!
: FUTAAAABAAAAAA!!! I FUCKING LOVE YOUUUUUUUUUUUUU!!!
: YOUR BOOBS RUUUULE!!!
: Kirin, come on. That’s totally uncalled for.
: ALL BOOBS RUUUUUULE!!! GO BOOOOOOBS!
: Oh yeah, that’s way better.
: This isn’t helping at all, is it?
: Boobs.
: Well...it looks like you might not have to work very hard, Touka. Futaba might bomb even worse than Tsuneyo at this rate.
: I still intend to give it my all regardless. It takes a great deal of courage to speak in front of others.
: Or at least that’s what I’ve been told. I’ve always found it rather easy, to be completely honest.
: Oh, it's totally hard. Like, when I started working at the mall, I could barely even talk to customers. I couldn’t even imagine having to speak in front of a whole crowd back then.
: It might be a little easier now because I’ve been working at the maid cafe for a while. Even still, though. Hard pass.
: If I am correct, Ami works at the maid cafe as well. Yes?
: Unfortunately, yes.
: I take it that you’ve had some...curious interactions with her as well then?
: “Curious” would be putting it nicely. But yes. My dislike for her became pretty intense around the time she started acting like she owned Sensei.
: Unless she’s the one who asked you to ask me about this. In which case, I change my answer to — she’s fine.
: She did not, no. I just believe that she may have some sort of problem with me based on a conversation we had earlier.
: You’re hot. She’s probably just mad that you’ve got double D’s and she doesn’t even have to use a bra yet.
: I do wonder if that’s all it is. I just felt as if her issues were slightly more pointed than breast envy alone.
: Could be. Are you in love with her dad by any chance?
: Love? Absolutely not.
: Yeah. I didn’t think so.
: I am interested in him, though.
: ...What?
: I imagine that’s strange to hear given the gap in both our respective ages and...net worths.
: And also because I imagine you’re quite intensely “in love” with him as well after nearly strangling Ami when she spoke about him in class.
: Are you going to dislike me too now?
: Am I...well...
: Touka, you practically gave me an apartment. And my sister’s quality of life is, like...way better now.
: So it’ll take more than you just...being interested in Sensei for me to dislike you.
: I see.
: And what if I were to sleep with him?
: Touka, I’d really prefer it if we don’t talk about this. I’m trying to not get involved in anyone’s romances but my own now.
: Doing the opposite is just...too painful.
: I completely understand and wholeheartedly apologize if that seemed crass of me. I don’t intend to ruin or disrupt any pre-existing relationship Sensei is involved in.
: This is likely just a hormonal issue on my end. I don’t mean to alarm you.
: Hormonal?
: Then, and this is purely hypothetical, do you think these feelings might go away if you did sleep with him?
: ...I’m sorry what?
: Like...and again, totally hypothetical, but say the three of us all got naked together and had sex in the same room-
: Chika, what has happened to you?
: Nothing. I’m normal.
: You don’t sound very normal right now.
: I’m totally normal and this is totally hypothetical. But you should still totally answer the question. Hypothetically, of course.
: Hm.
: Hypothetically?
: Then...
: Perhaps.
: Entirely hypothetically, of course.
: Oh yeah. Entirely. Which is why I’m definitely not going to hypothetically remember or hypothetically try and arrange it.
: Please hypothetically don’t.
: So...do?
: I’m actually not sure anymore as this conversation is bordering on the line of unintelligibility.
: Regardless, we should likely cease as it appears that Futaba is finally ready to begin.
: I completely and hypothetically agree.
: So you...don’t agree?
: I’m also not really sure what’s going on anymore.
: So, umm...hi.
: That...that part isn’t a joke.
: And t...to be com...pletely honest...there might not be any jokes while I’m up here because the...only joke I...thought up was just...me.
: Boooo! No self-deprecating humor! You are cherished and loved by all!
: ESPECIALLY ME! FUTABA RULES!
: Thank you, Rin...
: Y...You know...Rin and I...have known each other for years now! And throughout that time, we’ve...been through a lot together...
: Some highs...some lows...some...things we probably shouldn’t talk about...
: But I think the...thing I’ll always remember the most is...uhm...
: The time we accidentally shoplifted from FamilyMart and thought the police were going to find us and...lock us away for life.
: And when I say “we,” I...mostly mean me. Because, as I’m...sure you all know, I’m...not exactly the most exciting person out there.
: I don’t break rules often. And that’s probably because I’m too busy...breaking chairs from...sitting on-
: Okay, seriously — stop. I tried to be playful about it the first time, but if you use this mic to stand up here and trash yourself, I’m actually going to suspend you.
: But...Miss Imai...there are lots of comedians who...tell jokes about themselves to-
: Yeah. Jokes. Would you laugh if I came up here and talked about the way I look for an entire set, Futaba? Knowing what you know about me — would you laugh at that?
: I...no...of course not...
: Then don’t subject the people who love you to that same thing. Do you understand?
: Yes, Miss Imai...
: If you can’t believe in yourself, believe in the people who do.
: You got this.
: Ahem! Sorry about that, folks! Little technical difficulty. Nothing to be concerned about. Futaba — if you’d like to proceed.
: So...um...uhh...
: What’s the deal with airline food?!
: Sorry about that, Senpai. I- oh. I leave for one second and you bag Nodoka. Fun.
: I didn’t bag her. She’s just...tired, I think.
: Tired and...not suicidal.
: I don’t think you have to worry about Nodoka doing something like that. She has too much left to contribute to society to kill herself.
: Yeah, so did Robin Williams and Anthony Bourdain and look what happened to them.
: True, but Nodoka doesn’t have depression.
: Are you a psychologist now? She was literally just talking about a death fascination a few minutes ago.
: Yes. But while you were gone, she told me something else. Something she doesn’t want me repeating back to you.
: And that something is enough for you to think she’s okay and not in any immediate danger?
: None that doesn’t come from just lying on me.
: Okay, Senpai. If you say so. You know her better than I do.
: Would you mind working your magic on Futaba next, though? I’m seriously going to break if I hear that girl say one more bad thing about herself.
: I’ve been trying to “work my magic” on her for years now and I’ve gotten nowhere. I think she’s just immune to it.
: Perfect. Another adolescent girl who grows up hating herself because of the way she looks. I’m sure that won’t have any long term negative impact on her.
: Or she’ll grow up to be an accomplished, beautiful woman who’s a complete joy to be around and also very good at sex.
: Aww, Senpai. That’s really cute and nice of you. But also extremely creepy because you’re talking about a student.
: Yeah, I immediately regretted saying all of that.
Futaba’s set doesn’t last much longer. She mostly just retells jokes she’s heard from other comedians.
And while it sucks for her that her original plan went up in flames at the hands of a woman who likes her too much, I do think it’s what was best for everyone.
It’s just...really depressing.
But now Touka’s on stage and there’s no way she can be as miserable as that.
: Class of 1-A! Hello and thank you so much for having me.
: It’s both an honor and and absolute delight to come up on the same stage that’s seen the likes of several amazing comedians like-
: Approximately thirty seconds of Ayane and...fifteen seconds of Tsuneyo the last time we did this?...
: But I suppose that doesn’t matter! After all, stand-up comedy is difficult.
: And I imagine standing up is difficult in general when you spend as much time with Sensei as Ayane does.
: Touka-
: Aaah! Yes, yes — rules and regulations. Something we all know Miss Imai is overly familiar with.
: Just like I’m overly familiar with my checkbook and Sensei is overly familiar with...
: Cleaning his sheets, I hope?
: Knowing him, though — chances are he leaves that to his beloved Ami! Who, contrary to popular belief, is actually a very nice girl!
: In fact, just earlier today, she had the courtesy to tell me she admired how I’ve never had to work for anything in my life!
: Which I may have been initially offended by, I’ll admit.

: But, after thinking about it a little more, I realized there’s probably no one more familiar with doing nothing than a girl who thinks it’s somehow difficult to care for a man whose only interests are...
: See, I don’t even know. What are Sensei’s interests, Ami? Could you tell us, please?
: Right! He doesn’t have any.

: But still — I understand your plight and how slaving over a hot stove for an hour each day is likely much harder than the ten hours of classes I take after school while you forget to do your freshman algebra homework.
: I’m not only here to talk about Ami, though. Which I’m sure you’re all very excited to hear given that barely any of you even want to talk to her now.
: So instead! Let’s talk about her dad. Let’s talk about Sensei.
: Do you know what he told me recently? That I’m like a mother to him. Can you believe that? A mother. I didn’t even know Sensei had a mother.
: I assumed he was some sort of alien life form or government experiment based on how everyone seems to fall for him for no reason whatsoever.
: Even Io likes him. Yumi likes him. And I imagine Yasu likes him too, but I haven’t fully learned how to speak her language yet and can’t ask her.
: I’ll let you know when I do, though. In fact, right this very moment, I have her taking part in a comprehensive course on expression that- what’s that? She’s right behind me?
: Damn. Touka ain’t half bad.
: Oh! Thank you so much for weighing in, Kirin! Everyone knows just how much the rest of the girls in our class look to you for guidance.
: In fact, you were one of the first people I started learning from after I transferred in. Which is probably why I’m revealing so much skin right now.
: A job well done then.
: Words she’s never heard from her parents.
: And now I’m sad.
: Girls, Sensei — I imagine you all came here today expecting both of us to completely bomb.
: And given the objectivity of comedy, I suppose that some of you may believe I have.
: But to me, comedy is more than just telling jokes. It is commentary on the world. Or a subject. Or anything that brings people together.
: And that’s the point of Dorm Wars too, isn’t it? To unite the class in ways in which we normally wouldn’t?
: Or am I just still not getting this whole commoner thing and the point really is just fighting for Sensei’s approval?
: If that is the point, fine.
: If that really is the point, I ask you all to kindly forget every single thing I said up here today. Except for one.
: The part where that guy over there said he sees me like a mom.
: And how fucking weird that will make him if he ever bangs me.
: Well...that went better than last time at least. Which isn’t saying the bar was set all that high.
: But even if I have several issues with Touka’s performance, I will acknowledge that her set made me feel exponentially less bad than Futaba’s did.
: I could also not, in good faith, give Futaba the win because half of her jokes were pulled straight from the mouth of Jerry Seinfeld.
: Sooooo...Touka?
: Yes. Touka wins. But-
: Splendid! Thank you all so much for listening to me speak!
: And Sensei...
: Keep your daughter on a tighter leash or I will tie one to her neck myself.
: Holy shit.
